observations: For an origin-centred square with side 0.00002 cm, the Go reference reports zero profiles and the Rust adapter reports one certified region at the probe resolution.
For a 1 cm square translated to (100000000,100000000) cm, the direct pinned Martensite call declines with certified area 1 versus closed form 0.
For a 0.01 cm square at the same offset, the Go reference reports one closed profile and the Rust adapter declines with a certification mismatch.
The same direct call against local Martensite main at 4b76a823 also declines with certified area 1 versus closed form 0.
scope: The Rust probe is a temporary diagnostic module, not a product acceptance test. The Go and Rust programs print results for the same five axis-aligned inputs. The direct kernel test reproduces the translated unit-square decline without the application adapter.
reproduction: From the Go checkout, run go-profile-oracle.go. For Rust, copy rust-profile-probe.rs.txt into crates/martensite/tests/sketch_prism/profile_parity_probe.rs, add a matching test module to crates/martensite/tests/sketch_prism.rs, and run cargo test --locked -p oblikovati-martensite --test sketch_prism profile_parity_probe -- --nocapture. Remove the temporary module after the run.
limitations: The diagnostic tests print observations and do not certify full profile parity.
Go tolerance and area-cutoff differences mean a single Martensite region alone cannot verify a legacy Go profile index.
The main checkout was tested locally at the recorded commit; this does not establish the current remote main after that commit.
kernel_main_reproduction: Place kernel-main-probe.rs.txt in a temporary Cargo binary crate using martensite-tkbo from the recorded Martensite checkout, and run cargo run --offline. The lockfile used is retained alongside the source.
